targets.name: HEALTH E ALLIED SERVICES PTY LTD

party_page.name: Health E Allied Services Pty Ltd

merger_description:
Ochre Health Pty Limited (**Ochre Health**) proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Health E Medical Pty Ltd (**HEM**) and Health E Allied Services Pty Ltd (**HEAS**) (collectively, **Health E**) (the **Acquisition**).

The acquirer, Ochre Health, supports independent doctors to provide general practice medical services around Australia. Ochre Health currently operates 72 medical centres and urgent care clinics located in the ACT, NSW, Queensland, Tasmania and Victoria, but in greater Geelong, Victoria.  Ochre Health Group’s medical recruitment business, Ochre Recruitment, also works with hospitals and medical practices across Australia to source and place locum and permanent doctors across a range of specialities. Ochre Health is majority owned and controlled by Genesis Capital, an Australian-based private equity firm that invests in businesses operating in the healthcare sector.

Health E operates a general practice medical clinic in Geelong West, Victoria (the **Geelong West clinic**). HEM provides facilities and administrative services to independent general practitioners and other medical and allied health providers from the Geelong West clinic. HEAS offers administrative services to third party allied health service providers that operate from the Geelong West clinic.

Ochre Health does not currently offer administrative services to third party allied health service providers similar to those provided by HEAS, save for as an ancillary service as part of its operation of its existing general practice medical centres.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular, there is no overlap in the
supply of general practice medical services, or in the supply of
administrative services to third party specialist medical providers, in
the Geelong area.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
